newsitem.title: UK: Siemens takes steps to ready debt for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Siemens takes steps to ready debt for EMU.

text.p: Engineering giant Siemens on Tuesday became Europe's first company to prepare its international long-term debt for a single European currency.

Bankers for Siemens said earlier on Tuesday the company launched three Eurobonds, in French francs, guilders and marks, which will be redenominated in euros after the third stage of European economic and monetary union, scheduled for January 1, 1999.
Bankers at firms involved said the offering was one of the strongest selling they had ever seen.
Siemens has not issued a syndicated fixed-income deal publicly for more than 25 years.

U.S. bank J.P. Morgan and German bank Deutsche Morgan Grenfell were joint arrangers on all three deals. Dutch bank ABN AMRO Hoare Govett was joint lead manager on the guilder bond with French bank Paribas involved in the franc deal.

The bonds were a 750 million mark offering to be priced at a yield spread of 17 basis points spread over German government bonds, a 2.5 billion franc deal to be priced 14 basis points over French OATs and a 500 million guilder deal to be priced 20 basis points over Dutch DSLs.
